subject: Biology
title: Body Fluids and Circulation
summary: Blood is a fluid connective tissue: plasma (55%) and formed elements (45%) — RBCs, WBCs and platelets. Lymph is a colourless fluid that drains tissue fluid back into blood and carries fats.
ABO and Rh blood groups depend on antigens on RBCs; mismatched transfusion or Rh incompatibility in pregnancy can be dangerous.
The human heart has four chambers and double circulation. Its beat is myogenic, started by the SA node (pacemaker), and the cardiac cycle takes about 0.8 s.
The ECG records the heart's electrical activity (P, QRS, T). Disorders include hypertension, coronary artery disease, angina and heart failure.

formulas.name: Plasma composition
formulas.formula: 90–92% water, 6–8% proteins (fibrinogen — clotting; globulins — defence; albumins — osmotic balance)

formulas.name: Formed elements counts
formulas.formula: RBC 5–5.5 million/mm³;  WBC 6000–8000/mm³;  platelets 1.5–3.5 lakh/mm³;  haemoglobin 12–16 g/100 mL

formulas.name: RBC facts
formulas.formula: made in red bone marrow; biconcave, no nucleus in most mammals; life span 120 days; destroyed in spleen (graveyard of RBCs)

formulas.name: WBC percentages
formulas.formula: neutrophils 60–65% (phagocytes);  lymphocytes 20–25% (B, T — immunity);  monocytes 6–8% (phagocytes);  eosinophils 2–3% (allergy, infections);  basophils 0.5–1% (histamine, serotonin, heparin)

formulas.name: ABO groups
formulas.formula: A: antigen A, anti-B;  B: antigen B, anti-A;  AB: both antigens, no antibodies (universal recipient);  O: no antigens, both antibodies (universal donor)

formulas.name: Rh incompatibility
formulas.formula: Rh⁻ mother + Rh⁺ foetus → mother makes anti-Rh antibodies → affects the next Rh⁺ foetus (erythroblastosis foetalis);  prevented by anti-Rh antibodies to the mother right after the first delivery

formulas.name: Clotting cascade
formulas.formula: injury → thrombokinase → prothrombin → thrombin (needs Ca²⁺) → fibrinogen → fibrin threads trap blood cells → clot

formulas.name: Double circulation
formulas.formula: pulmonary: right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary veins → left atrium;  systemic: left ventricle → aorta → body → venae cavae → right atrium

formulas.name: Conducting system
formulas.formula: SA node (right upper atrium, 70–75 impulses/min, pacemaker) → AV node → bundle of His → right and left bundle branches → Purkinje fibres
formulas.note: The heart is myogenic: the impulse starts in the heart muscle itself.

formulas.name: Cardiac cycle
formulas.formula: duration = 60/heart rate ≈ 0.8 s at 72 beats/min;  atrial systole 0.1 s, ventricular systole 0.3 s, joint diastole 0.4 s

formulas.name: Cardiac output
formulas.formula: cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate ≈ 70 mL × 72 ≈ 5 L/min

formulas.name: Heart sounds
formulas.formula: lub (first): closure of tricuspid and bicuspid (AV) valves;  dub (second): closure of semilunar valves

formulas.name: ECG waves
formulas.formula: P: atrial depolarisation;  QRS: ventricular depolarisation (start of ventricular contraction);  T: ventricular repolarisation (end of systole)
formulas.note: Heart rate = number of QRS complexes per minute.

examples.title: Cardiac output
examples.problem: Stroke volume is 70 mL and heart rate 72 beats/min. Cardiac output?

examples.title: Duration of one cycle
examples.problem: Heart rate is 72 beats/min. How long is one cardiac cycle?

examples.title: Universal donor
examples.problem: Why is group O called the universal donor?
examples.solution: O RBCs carry no A or B antigens, so the recipient's antibodies don't agglutinate them.

examples.title: Erythroblastosis foetalis
examples.problem: An Rh⁻ woman carries her second Rh⁺ child. What is the risk?
examples.solution: Anti-Rh antibodies made after the first delivery cross the placenta and destroy the foetal RBCs — fatal anaemia and jaundice (erythroblastosis foetalis).

examples.title: Lymph and fat
examples.problem: Which vessels absorb fats from the intestine?
examples.solution: Lacteals (lymph vessels in the villi). Lymph carries the fat and drains into veins via the thoracic duct.

examples.title: Heart blocked at AV node
examples.problem: What happens if the AV node fails?
examples.solution: Impulses from the SA node can't reach the ventricles normally; ventricles beat at their own slower rate (heart block), needing an artificial pacemaker.

topics.title: Blood platelets and WBCs
topics.explain: Platelets (thrombocytes) are cell fragments from megakaryocytes in bone marrow and release clotting factors. A fall in their number causes clotting disorders and excessive blood loss.

topics.title: Lymph (tissue fluid)
topics.explain: As blood passes through capillaries, some water and small solutes move into tissue spaces, forming interstitial fluid; it has the same mineral distribution as plasma. Lymphatic vessels collect it and return it to major veins. Lymph contains lymphocytes.

topics.title: Open and closed circulation
topics.explain: Open: blood pumped into open spaces (arthropods, molluscs). Closed: blood always flows in vessels (annelids, chordates) — more precise regulation.

topics.title: Human heart structure
topics.explain: Mesodermal origin, in the thoracic cavity, slightly tilted left, enclosed in double-walled pericardium. Interatrial and interventricular septa; tricuspid (right) and bicuspid/mitral (left) AV valves; semilunar valves at the pulmonary artery and aorta openings.

topics.title: Regulation of cardiac activity
topics.explain: Heart activity is auto-regulated by nodal tissue but moderated by the medulla oblongata: sympathetic nerves increase rate and strength; parasympathetic (vagus) decreases them. Adrenal medulla hormones increase cardiac output.

topics.title: Disorders
topics.explain: Hypertension (high blood pressure — damages heart, brain, kidneys); coronary artery disease or atherosclerosis (deposits of calcium, fat and cholesterol narrow coronary arteries); angina pectoris (chest pain from insufficient O₂ to heart muscle); heart failure (heart can't pump enough blood — congestion of lungs). Cardiac arrest is when the heart stops beating; heart attack is when heart muscle is damaged by sudden lack of blood.

topics.title: Hepatic portal system
topics.explain: The hepatic portal vein carries blood from the intestine to the liver before it reaches the systemic circulation. Coronary circulation supplies the heart muscle itself.

ratta: AB universal recipient;  O universal donor.
P atrial depol.;  QRS ventricular depol.;  T ventricular repol.
Lub = AV valves close;  dub = semilunar valves close.
